To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Shoptalk interface can be used to solve problems in a manner similar to the manner in which they are solved in the factory.

(1) a direct manipulation style of interaction is more effective than a natural language style of interaction in supporting users of simulation in the process of scenario evaluation and (2) the effectiveness of a natural language interface is enhanced by the use of an integrated interface, in which natural language processing is used as a complement to direct manipulation.
the Shoptalk interface is a useful and usable tool to support factory command-and-control, and that the key to this is the integration of direct manipulation with natural-language processing.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how to make simulation more useful in the short-term decision-making process, particularly for managers and other decision-makers who need to understand the implications of alternative courses of action.
the problem of providing decision-support with simulations.
the problem of developing a user interface for a simulation model that supports the use of the simulation model for decision support.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper is a good one.
the Shoptalk interface is an excellent example of a system which is designed to support decision-making in an environment in which there are a large number of interacting objects.
this paper is a well written, clearly argued, interesting, and useful piece of work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Shoptalk interface is designed to support users who need to understand the simulation, to understand the problem, to make changes to the problem, to understand the consequences of the changes, and to communicate with others.
the use of direct manipulation and natural language in the same interface is a powerful combination.

we are developing a new style of interface for simulation, one that is more natural for managers and decision makers, that is more flexible for the simulation modeler, and that supports a new style of problem-solving, one that is characteristic of factory command-and-control and military command-and-control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the graphical user interface is not a panacea for all simulation needs, especially when the users are not simulation experts.
a graphical user interface is a good idea, but not the best idea.
a user interface can be built that is more natural and more flexible than a traditional graphical user interface.
